term.sleepStress.name: High sleep stress
term.sleepStress.line: The share of your night with heart-rate surges well above that night's usual sleeping heart rate.
term.sleepStress.body: OpenHoop cuts your night into 5-minute windows and finds the usual sleeping heart rate of that night. A window counts as high when it sits at least two spreads above it, the same step the daytime stress score calls high. Lower is better. Late meals, alcohol, illness and a warm room can all raise it.
term.restorative.name: Restorative
term.restorative.line: The share of your sleep spent in deep and REM sleep.
term.restorative.body: Deep sleep and REM sleep as a share of your time asleep. In healthy adults the two stages together usually take about a third to half of the night. It comes from the sleep stages, so it has their limits.
term.latency.name: Latency
term.latency.line: How long it took from the start of the night to the first sleep stage.
term.latency.body: The time from the start of your night to the first epoch scored as sleep. Up to 30 minutes is normal. It comes from the sleep stages, so it has their limits.
term.disturbances.name: Disturbances
term.disturbances.full: Times you woke up in the night
term.disturbances.line: How often the sleep stages show you awake between falling asleep and waking up.
term.disturbances.body: Each stretch scored as awake between your first and last sleep of the night counts once, however short. Most people wake briefly several times a night without remembering it.
